subject.title: [Feature]: Suppress or throttle transient channel connection status system events

question: Should OpenClaw hide or coalesce routine WhatsApp/channel connected-disconnected lifecycle notices by default, and what config/default policy should preserve operator-action notices?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the remaining work changes prompt-visible session context and likely adds config/default behavior, so automation should not pick the product contract alone.

options.title: Approve default-compatible WhatsApp policy
options.body: Add a WhatsApp-owned policy that keeps current behavior by default or uses a clearly approved default, coalesces short outages, and preserves terminal/operator-action notices with tests.

options.title: Keep current lifecycle notices
options.body: Treat these events as intentional operational context and close or narrow the request to documentation and dropped-message recovery work.

options.title: Design generic channel contract first
options.body: Pause the WhatsApp-only change and define a plugin SDK lifecycle-notification contract for all reconnecting channel plugins before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible WhatsApp policy
recommendation.body: Add a WhatsApp-owned policy that keeps current behavior by default or uses a clearly approved default, coalesces short outages, and preserves terminal/operator-action notices with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history across the shared system-event queue, config/docs surface, and WhatsApp runtime seams, making them the best available routing candidate for the policy call.
